Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-2-prompt-long-0120", "row_sha256": "f719bf0e5a6342f7c9e289159952d0872a04f2d927987aacc7bb03f422f31f21", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, can you put together a self-contained update about the ventilation check at the North Quay community workshop, the one on Alder Street. this is for the facilities team and the shop instructors, not a formal compliance certificate and not a recommendation about whether the shop can stay open. The check happened on 14 May, during the normal afternoon session, and the update should say that up front. Please make it readable for people who know the room but may not have been there that day. We need a useful record of what was looked at and what was actually seen, not a general explanation of ventilation.

The main work area is the fabrication room, where there are two flexible extraction arms over the bench, one fixed wall exhaust fan near the paint-preparation corner, and a rectangular supply-air grille above the double doors. The two arms are called the north arm and south arm in the maintenance notes, so keep those names rather than renaming them. The small wood room off the east side was not part of the check, and neither were the office, kiln room, or the extraction system serving the laser cutter. Please make that boundary easy to spot in the update because people sometimes assume the whole building got checked when they hear “ventilation check.” We only have notes for the fabrication room equipment described here.

At the time, the room was in ordinary use for a woodwork session with six people present. The north arm was in use for sanding, and the south arm was parked beside the bench with its damper shut. The wall fan was running and the supply grille was unobstructed. The exterior doors were closed; the double doors between the fabrication room and the corridor were open for the session. The check was not done with the room empty or with every system running at once, so include those operating details alongside the observations instead of turning them into a claim about every possible setup. The instructors had moved a rolling cabinet about half a metre from its usual marked position to make room for a delivery. That is worth mentioning as a condition on the day, but don't say it caused anything.

The notes have air-speed readings taken at the opening of each extraction arm while the north arm was running and the south arm was parked. They read 0.38 m/s at the north arm and 0.41 m/s at the south arm. There is no supplied pass/fail threshold or design figure to compare these readings against, so include the numbers with their locations and don't call them acceptable, low, high, or compliant. A separate reading at the supply grille was 0.22 m/s. It was taken at the centre of the grille with the wall fan running and the room doors in the positions I described. Don't combine that with the arm readings as if it were the same measurement. The notes don't give a repeat reading, instrument model, calibration date, or measurement uncertainty, so don't fill those gaps in or imply there was a full instrument report.

The visual notes say that the north arm moved through its full range without catching, and its hood stayed attached while it was positioned over the sanding bench. The south arm's outer hose had a small crease near its joint, but the notes do not say the crease blocked airflow or affected the reading. The wall fan grille had a thin layer of dust on the lower edge; it was still running during the check. The supply-air grille had no visible obstruction. Please report these as observations, not as a diagnosis or as proof that anything needs repair. No panels were opened and no ductwork was inspected, so the update shouldn't suggest the inside of the fan or ducts was checked.

For background, the maintenance log says the south arm was adjusted on 3 April after a user reported that it drifted away from the bench. The log records that adjustment but does not say the problem was tested again afterward. One of the instructors, Mara, said, “the south arm is the one that wandered before, but it stayed where I put it today.” Keep her words as a short ordinary quote and identify her as an instructor; don't convert the quote into a verified maintenance finding. The facilities coordinator has asked for this update before the next instructor meeting, but there isn't a meeting date in the notes. There's also no record here of a repair request, a follow-up booking, or a decision to change how the room is used.

Could you give the update a plain title and use connected paragraphs, with a numbered section for the recorded readings if that fits naturally. Cover the date and purpose, the equipment and boundaries of the check, the room conditions, the readings, and the visual observations. Keep the detail about the earlier south-arm adjustment and Mara's quote in a short context paragraph. Avoid adding general safety guidance, legal language, invented measurements, causes, recommendations, or a claim that the check passed. Please don't treat the information we don't have as evidence for or against the equipment. It's important that the update distinguish what was measured from what was only observed and make clear that this was a limited check of specified equipment in the fabrication room.

For the final section, include the complete assessment from the notes, without broadening it: at the time of the visit, the check recorded the listed air-speed readings and visual observations under the operating conditions above; it did not establish performance against a supplied acceptance criterion and did not include inspection inside the fan or ductwork. Keep the conditions attached to that assessment, including which arm was operating, the door positions, and the occupied afternoon session. End with a separate paragraph saying only that the notes contain no follow-up booking or room-use decision and that the facilities coordinator requested the update ahead of the next instructor meeting, whose date is not recorded. Don't turn that closing information into a proposed action or a summary judgment.", "output": "Write a self-contained, plain-language update for the North Quay community workshop facilities team and shop instructors about the ventilation check conducted on 14 May during the normal afternoon session. This is a record of the specified observations and measurements, not a formal compliance certificate or a recommendation about whether the shop can remain open. Use a plain title and connected paragraphs, with a numbered section for the recorded readings if useful.

Describe the scope clearly. The check covered the fabrication room’s two flexible extraction arms over the bench, the fixed wall exhaust fan near the paint-preparation corner, and the rectangular supply-air grille above the double doors. Use the maintenance-note names “north arm” and “south arm.” State that the small wood room off the east side, office, kiln room, and laser-cutter extraction system were not checked. Do not imply that the whole building was assessed.

Report the conditions during the check: the fabrication room was in ordinary use for a woodwork session with six people present; the north arm was being used for sanding; the south arm was parked beside the bench with its damper shut; the wall fan was running; and the supply grille was unobstructed. The exterior doors were closed, while the double doors between the fabrication room and corridor were open. Note that a rolling cabinet had been moved about half a metre from its usual marked position to make room for a delivery. Do not suggest that this change caused any observed or measured condition, or generalize the findings to other operating setups.

Include a numbered readings section, keeping the measurements distinct and their conditions clear:
1. With the north arm running and the south arm parked, the reading at the north arm opening was 0.38 m/s and the reading at the south arm opening was 0.41 m/s.
2. The supply-grille reading was 0.22 m/s, taken at the grille centre with the wall fan running and the doors in the positions described above.

No pass/fail threshold or design figure was supplied. Report the numbers without characterizing them as acceptable, low, high, or compliant, and do not combine the grille measurement with the arm readings. The notes contain no repeat reading, instrument model, calibration date, or measurement uncertainty; do not supply or imply any of those details or describe the notes as a full instrument report.

Describe the visual observations without turning them into a diagnosis, repair finding, or recommendation. The north arm moved through its full range without catching, and its hood stayed attached while positioned over the sanding bench. The south arm’s outer hose had a small crease near its joint; the notes do not say that it blocked airflow or affected the reading. The wall fan grille had a thin layer of dust on its lower edge and was running during the check. The supply-air grille had no visible obstruction. No panels were opened and no ductwork was inspected, so do not imply that the inside of the fan or ducts was checked.

In a short context paragraph, note that the maintenance log records an adjustment to the south arm on 3 April after a user reported that it drifted away from the bench. The log does not record a later test of the problem. Identify Mara as an instructor and include her statement as a short, ordinary quote: “the south arm is the one that wandered before, but it stayed where I put it today.” Do not present her comment as a verified maintenance finding.

In the final assessment section, preserve the full scope and conditions: at the time of the visit, the check recorded the listed air-speed readings and visual observations under the stated operating conditions; it did not establish performance against a supplied acceptance criterion and did not include inspection inside the fan or ductwork. Keep attached the fact that the north arm was operating while the south arm was parked, the door positions, and the occupied afternoon session. Do not broaden the assessment, invent a pass or failure, or add general safety guidance, legal language, causes, or recommendations.

End with a separate paragraph stating only that the notes contain no follow-up booking or room-use decision, and that the facilities coordinator requested the update ahead of the next instructor meeting, whose date is not recorded. Do not turn that information into a proposed action or a summary judgment."}]
